next_step: Complete 2-week high-qps pilot; finalize SLA addendum
notes: Account background: mid-market SaaS (customer support platform) with multi-tenant KB per customer.
Scope: moderate indexing scale — initial corpus ~1.2M docs (avg ~500 tokens) -> ~1.2M vectors; expect growth to ~3M in 12 months.
Traffic profile: high QPS target for hosted offering — pilot target 250 sustained QPS, 700 peak QPS across burst windows.
Latency & quality targets: P95 end-to-end reranking pipeline (embed + ANN + rerank) <120ms; P50 <60ms. Accepts some tail degradation if fallback triggers.
Cost sensitivity: target blended cost < $0.015 per query for average surfacing + rerank (must include embed + ANN + transformer rerank steps).
Model preferences: open to mid-sized Llama-family variants for rerank; embeddings: dense 1536-2048 dim. Want Redwood recommendations on quantization and batching.
Routing/fallback: primary hosted model for SLA customers; want policy to route lower-cost model for background/low-priority queries.
Security: must support SSO/SAML for internal tooling, SOC2 compliance required, audit logging + KMS integration for keys.
Quote from CTO: "We can tolerate a small drop in answer quality for low-value queries but cannot for escalations — need deterministic fallback policy."
POC notes: demo 2026-02-12 — validated indexing speed (120k docs/hour with current pipeline), measured ANN recall baseline. Next: run 2-week high-QPS pilot with sample tenant traffic.
Integration notes: planning to use Redwood SDK + existing Pinecone index for hybrid evaluation (vector store abstraction in front of Redwood reranker).
Legal/commercial: procurement asked for SLA addendum and explicit data residency clause for EU customers (likely 3rd quarter ask).
